Fine Dining Twist to Traditional Dishes in the Most Unexpected of Places!!!!
Feb 2016 • Friends
Whilst wandering about the small alleys of Pham Ngu Lao, the Typewriter hotel caught my eye.. Unlike other frumpy cheap backpacker hostels in the area, Tripwriter stands out with its modern take on French Indochine style. A quick look of the Bistro's menu revealed that there's much more to be explored (with my stomach).

I was travelling with a group of friends from America, China and Australia so had the opportunity to sample many of their dishes. In fact, we ordered almost everything from the menu! Hey it was a long day, we deserved it.

Honestly, many of the dishes, including fried rice, prawn cakes, egg rolls and steak were all rather common. They could be found almost anywhere in Vietnam. However, what distinguishes this Bistro from others is its level of care and creativity apparent in every single dish. The fried rice included dried rice which made the texture more crunchy while the steak included a sour salt that was absolutely divine. I was lucky to have the opportunity to speak to the head chef that day.

Mr. Vu, a former architect who gave up his career to pursue his passion in food proudly shared with me that he personally travels to Buan Ma Thuat to secure this special salt. The reason it's sour? Because it's comprised of ants! This may sound strange but I encourage you to try it, you may find it quite appetizing, as we all did.

All in all, a great experience! Very high quality food, with a unique take to traditional Vietnamese cuisine in the most unexpected of places. I wholeheartedly recommend all travelers in the are to seek out Mr Vu's Bistro at Typewriter, you will not be disappointed!!!

Incredible food, an oasis of calm!
Dec 2015 • Solo
This boutique hotel / restaurant is right in the midst of backpacker central however you walk off the street into an oasis of tranquility and style. No blaring music, flashing lights or people downing 2-for-1 cocktails, just peace. 
The food is unlike anything else you'll get in the area. Real Vietnamese flavours from all over the country. I had green mango salad with dried frogs (!!) and they were delicious. The pumpkin salad was also incredible. 
Staff are courteous and speak wonderful English. I stayed at the hotel also and they cannot do enough to help. I loved everything about this place and would come back tomorrow!
